summary: Use a Dropdown Input in a form when people choose one option from a list of four or more.

useWhen.text: In a form, when people choose one option from a list of four or more.

from.quote: Use a Dropdown Input in a form when people choose one option from a list of four or more.

avoidWhen.text: Two options, such as Yes or No: in a list they need an extra tap to see both answers.

from.quote: Yes or No needs an extra tap to see both answers.

anatomy.holds: Names the question the field answers (label).

from.quote: Names the question the field answers.

anatomy.holds: Pressable surface that opens the list; it shows the current choice and a chevron.

from.quote: Pressable surface that opens the list.

anatomy.holds: Tells people what to choose until they have chosen (placeholder); the choice replaces it.

from.quote: Tells people what to choose until they have chosen.

anatomy.holds: Shows that the field opens a list.

from.quote: Shows that the field opens a list.

anatomy.holds: Explains the choice (supportText), or the error when invalid (errorMessage).

from.quote: Explains the choice, or the error when invalid.

placementAdvice.text: Place it in a form, such as the In context transfer form, where From and To fields sit above a Continue button.

from.quote: Use a Dropdown Input in a form

placementAdvice.text: The field fills its container and is 48 px tall.

from.quote: The field fills its container and is 48 px tall.

placementAdvice.text: The field narrows with its column; the chevron stays at the end.

from.quote: The field narrows with its column; the chevron stays at the end.

placementAdvice.text: Pressing the field opens a Dropdown of the options just below it, as a layer over the page.

from.quote: Pressing it opens a Dropdown of the options just below.

placementAdvice.text: The open list matches the field’s width and scrolls after about five options.

from.quote: The open list matches the field’s width and scrolls after about five options.

placementAdvice.text: In the package the list opens below the field by default (placement bottom) and moves to the other side when there isn't room.

from.quote: Every field has a label.

configuration.text: A label and a placeholder are the minimum for a clear field.

from.quote: The minimum for a clear field.

configuration.text: Add support text when people need help choosing; it sits under the field.

from.quote: support text when people need help choosing.

configuration.text: Pass the options as items; the chosen option's label replaces the placeholder in the field.

from.quote: The choice replaces the placeholder.

configuration.text: The screen owns each value: pass value and update it in onValueChange, and check the form when people continue.

from.quote: The screen owns each value and checks the form when people continue.

configuration.text: Leave the list closed until people press the field (open and defaultOpen are left unset).

from.quote: Label the question, show the choice, and open the list only when asked.

configuration.text: Mark a field the form needs with isRequired: an asterisk follows the label.

from.quote: An asterisk follows the label.

configuration.text: When a field is invalid (isInvalid), errorMessage replaces the support text.

from.quote: Invalid replaces the support text with the error

configuration.text: Mark an empty field invalid when people continue, and show how to fix it.

from.quote: It marks an empty field invalid and shows how to fix it.

configuration.text: Use isReadOnly to show a value that cannot change right now.

from.quote: shows a value that cannot change right now.

configuration.text: It works with or without a safe-area provider at the app root.

from.quote: It works with or without a SafeAreaProvider.

rules.text: Write the label as a noun for the thing being chosen, such as “Account” or “Transfer from”.

from.quote: Write the label as a noun for the thing being chosen

rules.text: Write the placeholder as an instruction that starts with a verb, such as “Select an account”.

from.quote: Add a placeholder that starts with a verb

rules.text: Write error messages as a way to fix the problem, such as “Choose an account to transfer from”.

from.quote: error messages as a way to fix the problem.

rules.text: Do not write a vague error: “Invalid” does not say what went wrong.

from.quote: “Invalid” does not say what went wrong.

rules.text: Keep a visible label: “Account” still explains the value after a choice, while a placeholder disappears once people choose.

from.quote: “Account” still explains the value after a choice.

good: Choose an account to transfer from

from.quote: The chosen option is announced as selected, invalid, required, and disabled are announced, a disabled field leaves the tab order, and focus shows a ring.

accessibility.text: accessibilityLabel names the field; without it the field is named by its label, then its placeholder.

examples.purpose: The guide's In context: choose accounts for a transfer. A Card holds a title, a From and a To field with the same four accounts, and a Continue button. The screen owns each value (value and onValueChange); when people continue it marks an empty field invalid (isInvalid) and its errorMessage says how to fix it.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <Text text="Transfer money" />
    <DropdownInput
      label="From"
      placeholder="Select an account"
      items={[
        { value: 'savings', label: 'Savings account' },
        { value: 'checking', label: 'Checking account' },
        { value: 'brokerage', label: 'Brokerage account' },
        { value: 'recurring', label: 'Recurring deposit' },
      ]}
      value={null}
      onValueChange={() => {}}
      errorMessage="Choose an account to transfer from"
    />
    <DropdownInput
      label="To"
      placeholder="Select an account"
      items={[
        { value: 'savings', label: 'Savings account' },
        { value: 'checking', label: 'Checking account' },
        { value: 'brokerage', label: 'Brokerage account' },
        { value: 'recurring', label: 'Recurring deposit' },
      ]}
      value={null}
      onValueChange={() => {}}
      errorMessage="Choose an account to transfer to"
    />
    <Button label="Continue" onPress={() => {}} />
  </VStack>
</Card>

from.quote: The screen owns each value and checks the form when people continue.

props.name: label
props.description: Label rendered above the input.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no value is selected. Default "Select an option", from the component source.

props.name: items
props.description: Data-driven list of options. Mutually compatible with `children`; if both are provided the `items` are rendered first.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected value (controlled). When `value` is `undefined` the component operates in uncontrolled mode and keeps its own state.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial selected value for uncontrolled mode. Default null, from the component source.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when the selected value changes.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom slot of `<DropdownItem />` children. Used when finer-grained control is needed (icons, custom layouts, etc.). When provided alongside `items`, both are rendered (items first).

props.name: renderValue
props.description: Custom renderer for the trigger label. Receives the currently-selected option (if any) and a boolean indicating whether the field has a value.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state for uncontrolled mode. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called whenever the open state changes.

props.name: placement
props.description: Preferred placement for the popup. The component falls back to the opposite side automatically when there isn't enough room. Default "bottom", from the component source.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Renders a required asterisk next to the label. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: On the web a disabled field has aria-disabled=true and tabindex=-1, so it is announced as disabled and leaves the tab order. Declared: Disables interaction and dims the field. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: isInvalid
props.description: Marks the field as invalid and shows `errorMessage`. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Renders the field in read-only mode (non-interactive but not disabled). Default false, from the component source.

props.name: supportText
props.description: Helper text displayed below the input.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Replaces `supportText` when `isInvalid` is true.

props.name: menuMaxHeight
props.description: Maximum height of the popup before it becomes scrollable. Helpful for long lists. Defaults to 240 (roughly 5 items). Default 240, from the component source.

props.name: menuOffset
props.description: Pixel gap between the trigger and the popup. When omitted, it defaults to the `formField/gap` design token so the menu sits the same distance below the input as the rest of the field's internal spacing.

props.name: matchTriggerWidth
props.description: When true, the popup width matches the trigger width. When false, the popup uses its intrinsic content width but never exceeds the trigger. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: closeOnBackdropPress
props.description: Whether tapping the backdrop closes the menu. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: modes
props.description: Modes for design token resolution.

props.name: style
props.description: Style overrides for the outermost wrapper.

props.name: inputStyle
props.description: Style overrides for the input row.

props.name: menuStyle
props.description: Style overrides for the popup container.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessibility label. Defaults to the visible label / placeholder.

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: Accessibility hint.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Called when the trigger receives focus (web only).

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Called when the trigger loses focus (web only).

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: When `true`, disables text truncation: the trailing ellipsis (`…`) is never shown and any `numberOfLines` clamp is ignored, so the text wraps to as many lines as it needs even when horizontal space is tight.
